title: Provisional measurement review
notice: These are newly derived, unvalidated educational observations. The source supplies no printed answer key for this exercise. They are unscored and require qualified ECG educator review.

fields.value: Spacing is visibly nonuniform in this short sample. Early intervals are 126, 131, 126 and 124 px, followed by 122, 115, 112 and 113 px; they generally shorten toward the right. Do not label strictly regular.
fields.basis: Provisional comparison of 8 complete positive peak-to-peak intervals in original PDF 437
fields.reason: Observed intervals: 126 px, 131 px, 126 px, 124 px, 122 px, 115 px, 112 px, 113 px. These describe this brief sample, not a validated rhythm classification.

fields.basis: Assumed course speed 25 mm/s; 151 grid lines enclose 150 small horizontal intervals across 1163 pixels.
fields.reason: 8 retained positive peak-to-peak intervals have mean spacing 121.12 px, giving 96.0 bpm. Individual-interval estimates span approximately 88.8–103.8 bpm under the same assumption; this is observed interval variation, not a confidence interval. No numerical speed label or labeled timing duration is verified on this strip. This is interval-derived, not a six-second beat count or a claim of a stable rate.

fields.value: Candidate P-wave observation: Four reviewed interior cycles each contain a distinct small positive pre-complex bump with a similar contour, separated from the sharp complex by a short low-amplitude segment. This supports a P-like visual observation, not validated atrial identity or proof of one-to-one conduction.
fields.basis: Original PDF page 437; repeated-complex visual review and independent source comparison
fields.reason: Provisional visible-deflection description, not validated atrial identity, atrial origin, or a diagnosis. Qualified ECG educator review is outstanding.

fields.basis: Original PDF page 437; independently reconciled endpoint bands and horizontal grid; assumes course 25 mm/s (0.04 s per small square), not a verified per-strip speed
fields.reason: P-like onset is bracketed independently from the sharp-complex onset on four interior cycles. The resulting geometric interval is a conditional PR candidate only if the small bump is confirmed as atrial activity; peaks are not used as onsets. Final approximate envelope covers both independent readers; not a confidence interval or physiologic variability. This envelope includes reader and endpoint uncertainty; it is not a confidence interval, normal/abnormal classification, or proof of beat-to-beat physiological variation.

fields.value: Nine repeated sharp positive peaks followed immediately by much deeper negative excursions. The first several negative excursions approach or meet the lower image border, so positive peaks are used consistently. Small rounded pre-peak bumps and broader between-complex deflections are visible; the latter change contour/polarity across the strip. These are visual descriptions, not validated P/T-wave identifications.
fields.basis: New descriptive observation of the original raster; not a source-authored rhythm diagnosis
fields.reason: No diagnostic rhythm label, validated P-wave identity, validated conduction interval or clinical conclusion is assigned. Conditional interval estimates, where present, remain unvalidated. Qualified ECG educator review has not occurred.

limitations: New wave-field estimates remain provisional and unscored. Range width reflects uncertain endpoints and reader disagreement, not a validated diagnostic category. QT/QTc, calibrated amplitudes and clinical diagnosis are not established.
The exact original PDF was checked. The inspected waveforms are embedded rasters; larger rendering does not add samples. Expert interpretation may still improve unresolved component identification.

QRS duration unresolved: Terminal return is curved and merges into a changing recovery segment. Candidate end bands are recorded, but the source does not establish a unique terminal depolarization/J-point boundary. Some troughs also approach the lower crop border. Do not promote the arithmetic span to a QRS-duration answer.
Small pre-peak bumps are visible, but atrial identity and conduction relationship are not independently validated.

The 150-small-interval span would be six seconds only under the assumed course convention. Unlabeled top marks do not independently verify that duration. Only measured horizontal spacing is used for time, not vertical pixel spacing.

Approximate ±2 source pixels per fiducial and ±0.15 pixels per grid pitch are illustrative sensitivity allowances, not confidence limits. They exclude unknown speed, source distortion and incorrect waveform identification.
A mean rate can conceal changing spacing. Read the regularity description and individual-interval range; no sustained rate or diagnostic rhythm is inferred.

Pink occupancy is threshold-sensitive because horizontal grid lines and antialiasing affect projections. Selected clean bands independently resolve matching line sequences, without inserted or imputed lines. Lower thresholds can merge lines; higher thresholds can miss faint lines. Those trial counts are not used as physical interval counts.
Initial and terminal low rounded humps are not counted as ventricular complexes.
Some early negative troughs approach or meet the lower crop border. Their extrema are not used; the corresponding complete positive peaks remain usable for spacing.
